newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares soar again to close at new highs.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares soar again to close at new highs.

text.p: Italian stocks closed sharply higher to set new closing records on Monday, ignoring weak performances on other stock markets and pushing up from early lows on a return of the wave of general euphoria seen last week.
Dealers said they saw buying by both domestic and foreign players and the market tone was positive despite the weight of 24 stocks trading ex-dividend.
Optimism over Italy's chances of joining the first wave of European monetary union and an expected low inflation figure for June kept the market buoyant.

The last of 11 sample Italian cities published their preliminary June consumer prices data after market closure on Monday, indicating inflation this month is running at 1.4 to 1.5 percent year on year compared with 1.6 percent in May.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 1.0 percent up at 13,317 and the Mib30 blue chip index ended 0.98 percent up at 20,236.
Dealers noted that closing indices would have been higher without the batch of ex-dividend stocks, weighing some 0.7 percent on bourse indices.
State-controlled energy group ENI, with its third tranche public share starting on Monday and going ex-dividend for 240 lire, slipped 0.72 percent to 9,400 lire in volume of over 41 million shares.

Troubled information and technology group Olivetti closed up 4.18 percent at 479 lire, financial holding Compart up 4.02 percent at 797 and in the telecoms sector, state holding Stet ended up 1.34 percent at 9,940.
Traded volume was estimated at nearly two trillion lire ($1.1 billion) against Friday's turnover of more than five trillion lire.
